Thanks for the clear options. A couple of clarifying questions before we run this internally:

Tim —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and great questions. Short answers up front, details below.

1) Usage shortfalls and true-up: Our standard handling is a true-up at month 12 that reconciles actuals vs committed consumption. For a 60/40 split we can add a capped pro-rated protection for the first 6 months: if year1 actuals are < 75% of forecasted year1 consumption, we allow a single pro-rata credit up to 15% of the year1 invoice (applies only to the 60/40 option). This is to reduce stranded spend while preserving the term economics that justify the 8% discount.

2) SLA credits vs term discount: SLA credits are operational (monthly service credits) and do not change the negotiated term discount — they operate as separate remedies in the MSA. We will not claw back the term discount for SLA credits, but material repeated breaches could trigger remediation defined in the SLA (and, in extreme cases, termination clauses).

3) Split invoices / POs: We can accept two year-specific POs. For accounting we will tag the invoices to the same contract number; the economics stay tied to the committed amount. I'll note that split billing requires one additional internal approval but is standard.

4) Step-down / early termination: Draft language attached (see approved_term_sheet_kp_1126.pdf). Proposed approach: 12-month lookback with a 9-month pro-rata clawback for amounts invoiced in the first 12 months, scaled by remaining months in term. Legal to review; Marissa — please confirm if this is ok to send to SlateBridge legal.

Next steps: if this is acceptable I can share a marked-up SOW and a DocuSign envelope with the 60/40 option pre-populated (SB-4721). Proposed call: Mon 11/09 11:00am PT for a 30-min alignment — Ben, can you join? Jordan, Marissa — FYI.
